memo:
EdgeHound Performance Review — 21 June 2026

The portfolio sits at -13.93% return on $10K start (equity $8,607), with realized P&L of -$1,477 across 147 settled trades. The loss is concentrated and attribution is clear: MOMENTUM (-$1,019, 8W/21T = 38% win rate) and SMART_CONSENSUS (-$385, 0W/1T) are responsible for the bulk of damage. Both correctly remain disabled per prior session.

SHORT_FAVORITE on high-priced sports markets remains the validated edge: 71% win rate (90% CI 62–79%), VALIDATED hypothesis, positive directional PnL on most individual resolved trades. The net -$339 in SHORT_FAVORITE PnL is driven by a handful of large stop-loss events (e.g., -$123, -$100, -$80, -$64) against a background of many small wins ($7–$29). This is structurally expected in a short-vig strategy — catastrophic individual losses offset many small wins. The Brier score of 0.248 is acceptable.

VOLUME_SPIKE (+$190, 8W/20T) and ELITE_FOLLOW (+$76, 12W/24T) are both marginally positive and worth retaining, though sample sizes remain small. ELITE_FOLLOW's Iran nuclear trade series showed both large wins and large losses — the $300–$350 stakes on geopolitical events are outsized for the current bank.

Key concern: open position Minnesota Twins at $500 stake is disproportionately large relative to the ~$8,600 equity base (~5.8%). With maxEventExposure at $750 and open Kansas City at $400, concentration in SHORT_FAVORITE sports at high stakes warrants monitoring. No parameter changes are warranted this session given recent adjustments and insufficient new settled data to justify further tuning.
